Build and ship

Build and export a game

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Native developmentDesktop exportsBrowser exportsServe the exported gameCheck the network deployment separately

The native editor and an exported game have different loading arrangements. Understand the build products before choosing an export target. Keep the SDK, Odin compiler, Godot engine, and export templates compatible with the checkout or addon release you are using.

Native development#

The core GDExtension loads a separately compiled scripts library. The normal repository build command compiles both:

Shell
bash build/build_scripts.sh /absolute/path/to/your_game

An installed addon can reuse its prebuilt core with SKIP_CORE=1. Generated registration and boot files are compiled with authored source. A successful compile is the first check; open the game and inspect the engine output for library or ABI errors.

Desktop exports#

The editor export plugin compiles scripts for the target and packages them with the core. Cross-target builds need the matching native toolchain. Use the export reference for presets, cross compilation, and the platform-specific evidence. The distribution guide distinguishes build verification from execution on a target machine.

Check the exported game itself. Opening a project in the editor does not exercise the exported library locations or prove that the target has all required assets.

Browser exports#

The web build links the extension and scripts into one Emscripten side module:

Shell
bash build/build_web.sh /absolute/path/to/your_game

Use a Web export preset with extension support and a compatible Emscripten toolchain. The repository's web instructions explain template compatibility, editor tool paths, manifest entries, and the actual export command.

Avoid native-only imports in code compiled for WASM. Store Godot instance IDs in the documented 64-bit type rather than pointer-sized Odin int. Web does not provide the native library reload path; inspect browser console output when debugging a web build.

Serve the exported game#

Godot web configurations that use shared memory require cross-origin isolation. The bundled local server supplies the relevant headers:

Shell
bash addons/odin_godot/build/serve.sh path/to/export_dir

Configure the same requirements on the production game host. On itch.io, use its SharedArrayBuffer support option for a build that needs it. The SDK documentation website is ordinary static HTML; serving the docs and serving a Godot game are separate hosting tasks.

Check the network deployment separately#

A local native host/client run does not establish internet reachability. Browser multiplayer needs an appropriate RTC/Party configuration. Plan signaling, relay or TURN policy, admission, identity storage, and trusted authority deployment according to the chosen runner. The small Replay starter's browser mode is offline until the game supplies that network configuration.

Use debugging for native failures and the examples' focused checks for input, correction, recovery, and browser workflows.
